findings.title: A late-check 504 carries the backend response headers (Set-Cookie, cacheable Cache-Control) into the error page
findings.description: The second throwIfFired runs after res.status(head.status) and applyResponseHeaders have copied the backend headers into res. Response has no API to remove headers, and the core error flow keeps headers that were already set. So the 504 that FND-001's fix now produces goes out with the backend's headers, among them Set-Cookie (a backend session cookie set on a gateway-timeout page) and Cache-Control: public, max-age=600 (a shared cache may store the 504 page for 10 minutes). Before this change the path never produced a 504. The leak is new, and it contradicts the change's own stated intent. The window is narrow in production (the header copy) but reachable, and it is the exact window the round's test targets.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not let a 504 go out after the backend headers were written into res. One option: move the last throwIfFired before res.status(head.status), after building the RelayedBodyStream and registering releaseOnAbort, so a deadline firing during the header copy counts as after the hand-off (FR-PROXY-016 abort). The other: collect the copied, rewritten and fixed headers into a list and apply them only after the final check. Add a test asserting the 504 has no backend headers.

findings.description: The new test stalls inside res.status(), so only the second check catches the deadline. With the first check removed, a deadline that fires during the head read is still turned into a 504 by the second check, but only after the backend headers have been set (see FND-101). So the first check is the one that keeps that case from leaking headers, and no test guards it.
